subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Mars Climate Orbiter: The Unit Conversion Error
description: Learn Mars Climate Orbiter: The Unit Conversion Error in one minute.

hook.text: On September 23, 1999, NASA's Mars Climate Orbiter burned up in the Martian atmosphere. It flew too low.

buildup.text: The spacecraft was supposed to orbit Mars at 150 km altitude. Instead, it entered the atmosphere at just 57 km.

discovery.text: Lockheed's software output thrust in pound-force seconds. NASA's expected newton-seconds. Nobody caught the mismatch.

twist.text: The $327 million spacecraft was destroyed by a unit conversion error that any physics student could have caught.

climax.text: NASA implemented mandatory unit verification procedures and interface control documents for all future missions.

punchline.text: Pounds vs. newtons. A $327 million rounding error.

quiz.question: What specific error destroyed the Mars Climate Orbiter?
options: A navigation antenna pointed in the wrong direction during orbit insertion
Thrust data was output in pound-force seconds but read as newton-seconds
The spacecraft's heat shield was designed for Venus, not Mars
